topics.topic: Caller identity and project-scoped authorization
questions: Is the bearer token bound to the owner, the calling flow, a machine installation, or a shared service identity, and how is authorization scoped to projects?
What principal and project permissions does the token represent, and what observable failure occurs for a missing, invalid or insufficient token?
What identity and authorization claims are bound to a request, and how does the deliverer ensure the caller may act on the supplied project id?

quotes:
Every operation except the health answer requires the deliverer's bearer token, compared in
   constant time. Any other value is refused before the request is handled.
There is one principal: the calling flow of the owner. It may act on every confirmed connection.
judgement.why: State 2 defines the principal, project authority, and authentication refusal.

topics.topic: Camera-date field precedence and timezone conversion
questions: What timezone is used to convert a camera timestamp that contains no offset into UTC?
Which metadata fields count as the camera record, in what precedence, and how are invalid or conflicting values handled?
Which camera date field wins, and what timezone or ambiguity rule converts a camera timestamp that contains no offset into UTC?
Which metadata fields count as the camera record, and what precedence applies when original, digitized and offset-bearing timestamps disagree?
Which timezone is used when the camera timestamp has no offset, and how are daylight-saving ambiguity and nonexistent local times resolved?

quotes:
The photo moment is the camera's original time, then the camera's general time, then the
   file's modification time. The first two count only when the year is 2000 or later and the
   moment is not more than one day after the file's modification time.

The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset (the Client Portal stores it this way). A camera time with
   no offset is read in the configured time zone.
| Camera time zone | Europe/Madrid | run setting |
judgement.why: State 2 decides field precedence, validity checks, and the timezone used for offsetless camera times.

topics.topic: Connection creation, confirmation, editing, and removal workflow
questions: What product action creates, confirms, changes or removes the object-to-folder connection required before delivery?
Where are the root folder, photo and invoice subfolders, object identity and owner confirmation supplied for creating the persistent connection?
Can a confirmed connection's folders be changed, and if so what happens to existing scans, source ids, placements and publication marks?
What concrete action creates the connection, what inputs and confirmation does it require, what does it return, and how can it fail?
Can a connection be edited, reconfirmed, disabled or removed; what happens to existing placement history when its folders or project id change; and what exactly makes it confirmed?
What concrete action creates, confirms, changes, disables or removes a connection, what validates its paths and project id, and what are the observable results and failures?

quotes:
Takes the photos, decides what a client sees and
  connects an object to its folder.

| See what can be delivered for a project | each file with a status: ready, placed, published, settling, duplicate or rejected with a reason | unknown project, unconfirmed connection or unavailable folder is refused; nothing is changed | unit tests, E2E |

One connection per object: its Registry project id, root folder, photo and invoice
  subfolders and the owner's confirmation.

One record per object, keyed by the Registry project id and confirmed by the owner, holds the
object's photo and invoice folders. The deliverer uses it now. The Cabinet Inbox moves to it
later as a separate step.
judgement.divergence: One implementation provides an owner-facing action that creates and confirms the connection; another requires an unstated out-of-band record and only refuses delivery, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The required connection and owner confirmation are named, but no current product action carries their creation or confirmation.

witness.initial: A Registry project exists without a confirmed connection.
events: The owner starts a delivery from the workplace.
The calling flow asks what can be delivered for the project.
outcomes: The product offers an action to enter the folders and confirm the connection, after which scanning can proceed.
The deliverer refuses the project and provides no product action by which the owner can resolve the refusal.
basis:
A delivery starts from an action of the owner in the workplace. The service delivers nothing
by itself.

It asks what can be
delivered, asks for placement, publishes in the Portal with the kernel's own Portal
session and tells the deliverer which Portal photo resulted.

questions: Does this action rescan the folder, use a cached scan, or return a snapshot, and how does the caller know when the observation was made?

topics.topic: Meaning and scope of human principals
questions: Is the client another human principal, or does “principal” mean only an actor authenticated to the deliverer?

topics.topic: Observable failure caused by unrepaired legacy dates
questions: What does "breaks" observably mean, which operation fails or corrupts data, and can the system detect affected projects without attempting a delivery?

topics.topic: Portal show and hide operations and reversibility
questions: What exact Portal state change makes a hidden photo visible, and is visibility reversible through a hide operation?
Which promise or action carries hiding a wrong or superseded photo, and what observable result and failure does that action have?

topics.topic: Purpose and access rules for the invoice subfolder
questions: Why is an invoice subfolder stored when R0-03 excludes expense documents, and may the deliverer inspect or expose it?

topics.topic: Uniqueness constraints for Portal photo identifiers
questions: May the same Portal photo id be recorded against two different placed sources or projects?

quotes: A publication mark: which Portal photo a placed source became.

A mark needs an existing placement of the same project, otherwise it is refused with
   `not_placed`.
judgement.why: Cross-placement uniqueness of Portal photo identifiers is a rule constraint, and the current rule only states placement ownership and same-source conflicts.

topics.topic: Whether background activity is allowed without an owner request
questions: May it scan folders, compute statuses, clean orphaned data or retry interrupted work without an owner action, or is every read and write prohibited until a request?

topics.topic: Whether listings include removed or replaced historical sources
questions: Does the result contain only files currently present, or also historical placed and published sources whose files were removed or replaced?

quotes: A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status.

The same placement is returned after the source file has left the folder
  (`test_placing_again_returns_the_same_result_without_writing`).
Removing a source changes no placement (R0-10).
judgement.why: State 2 makes listings observations of currently present regular files while preserving removed sources only in durable placement history.
